questions.question: Define HTTP and state its default port number in WWW architecture. (K, CO1)
questions.solution_html:
• Answer: (1 mark for each step; any five)
  • • The user enters a URL in the browser (client) or clicks a hyperlink (1 mark).
  • • The domain name in the URL is resolved to the server’s IP address using DNS (1
  • mark).
  • • The browser opens a TCP/IP connection with the web server (default port 80) (1
  • mark).
  • • The browser sends an HTTP request containing the method (GET/POST), the
  • requested resource and request headers (1 mark).
  • • The web server processes the request, locating the file or running a server -side
  • script such as PHP (1 mark).
  • • The server returns an HTTP response with a status code (e.g. 200 OK, 404 Not
  • Found), response headers and the content (HTML, images, etc.) (1 mark).
  • • The browser renders the page; the connection is closed since HTTP is a stateless
  • request–response protocol (1 mark).

questions.question: Explain the structure of an HTML table using <table>, <tr>, <th>, and <td> tags, and provide a suitable example.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine why the database name is required in mysqli_connect() even though host and
  • username are given.
  • Answer: (1 mark for each point)
  • • Syntax: mysqli_connect(host, username, password, database); it returns a
  • connection object, or false on failure (1 mark).
  • • Host and username (with password) only locate the MySQL server and
  • authenticate the user; they do not identify which data is to be used (1 mark).
  • • One MySQL server holds many databases; the database name selects the default
  • database on which all subsequent queries through that connection operate (1
  • mark).
  • • Without a selected database, queries on unqualified table names fail with a “No
  • database selected” error; the database would then have to be chosen with
  • mysqli_select_db($conn, "dbname") or every table written as dbname.table (1
  • mark).
  • • Giving it in mysqli_connect() connects and selects in one step, limits the script to
  • the intended database and simplifies error checking with mysqli_connect_error()
  • typically in a reusable connection file (1 mark).
  • Reference example
  • $conn = mysqli_connect("localhost", "root", "", "college");
  • if (!$conn) {
  • die("Connection failed: " . mysqli_connect_error());
  • }
  • $result = mysqli_query($conn, "SELECT * FROM student");

questions.question: Execute the steps required to configure XAMPP and run a PHP script on a local Apache server. (A, CO2)
questions.solution_html:
• Answer: (1 mark for each step)
  • • Start the MySQL server (XAMPP Control Panel) and open the MySQL client
  • phpMyAdmin or a PHP connection using mysqli_connect() (1 mark).
  • • Create and select the database: CREATE DATABASE college; USE college; (1
  • mark).
  • • Create the table with CREATE TABLE, specifying column names, data types and
  • constraints such as PRIMARY KEY / NOT NULL (1 mark).
  • • Add one record with INSERT INTO table (columns) VALUES (values); string
  • values in quotes (1 mark).
  • • Execute and verify, e.g. run the statements through mysqli_query() and check its
  • return value, and confirm the record using SELECT (1 mark).
  • Reference example
  • CREATE DATABASE college;
  • USE college;
  • CREATE TABLE student (
  • roll_no INT PRIMARY KEY
  • name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
  • marks INT
  • );
  • INSERT INTO student (roll_no, name, marks) VALUES (1, 'Anu', 85);
  • SELECT * FROM student;

questions.question: Examine why the database name is required in mysqli_connect() even though host and username are given.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine why the database name is required in mysqli_connect() even though host and
  • username are given.
  • Answer: (1 mark for each point)
  • • Syntax: mysqli_connect(host, username, password, database); it returns a
  • connection object, or false on failure (1 mark).
  • • Host and username (with password) only locate the MySQL server and
  • authenticate the user; they do not identify which data is to be used (1 mark).
  • • One MySQL server holds many databases; the database name selects the default
  • database on which all subsequent queries through that connection operate (1
  • mark).
  • • Without a selected database, queries on unqualified table names fail with a “No
  • database selected” error; the database would then have to be chosen with
  • mysqli_select_db($conn, "dbname") or every table written as dbname.table (1
  • mark).
  • • Giving it in mysqli_connect() connects and selects in one step, limits the script to
  • the intended database and simplifies error checking with mysqli_connect_error()
  • typically in a reusable connection file (1 mark).
  • Reference example
  • $conn = mysqli_connect("localhost", "root", "", "college");
  • if (!$conn) {
  • die("Connection failed: " . mysqli_connect_error());
  • }
  • $result = mysqli_query($conn, "SELECT * FROM student");

questions.question: Illustrate the complete data retrieval and modification process for a Student table. (a) Explain SELECT and write queries to retrieve all records and only name and marks. (b) Write a SELECT query with WHERE to list students scoring more than 75. (c) Write an UPDATE and a DELETE query, explaining WHERE in both.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain SELECT and write queries to retrieve all records and only name and marks. (b)
  • Write a SELECT query with WHERE to list students scoring more than 75. (c) Write an
  • UPDATE and a DELETE query, explaining WHERE in both.
  • Answer: (a) 6 marks; (b) 4 marks; (c) 5 marks. Assume Student(roll_no, name, marks).
  • (a) SELECT (6 marks)
  • • SELECT retrieves data (rows/columns) from one or more tables; the result is
  • returned as a result set (1 mark).
  • • Syntax: SELECT column1, column2 | * FROM table_name
  • [ORDER BY column]; – * selects all columns (1 mark).
  • • Retrieve all records: SELECT * FROM Student; (2 marks).
  • • Retrieve only name and marks: SELECT name, marks FROM Student; (2 marks).
  • (b) SELECT with WHERE (4 marks)
  • • Query: SELECT * FROM Student WHERE marks > 75; (3 marks; also accept
  • SELECT name, marks FROM Student WHERE marks > 75;).
  • • Explanation: WHERE filters the rows, so only students whose marks exceed 75 are
  • listed (1 mark).
  • (c) UPDATE and DELETE (5 marks)
  • • UPDATE query: UPDATE Student SET marks = 80 WHERE roll_no = 3;
  • modifies existing values (2 marks).
  • • DELETE query: DELETE FROM Student WHERE roll_no = 5; – removes matching
  • rows (2 marks).
  • • Role of WHERE in both: it restricts the change to the rows that satisfy the
  • condition; if WHERE is omitted, UPDATE changes every row and DELETE
  • removes all rows of the table (1 mark).
  • Optional PHP illustration of the process
  • $conn = mysqli_connect("localhost", "root", "", "college");
  • $result = mysqli_query($conn, "SELECT name, marks FROM Student WHERE marks
  • > 75");
  • while ($row = mysqli_fetch_assoc($result)) {
  • echo $row["name"] . " - " . $row["marks"] . "
    ";
  • }
  • mysqli_query($conn, "UPDATE Student SET marks = 80 WHERE roll_no = 3");
  • mysqli_query($conn, "DELETE FROM Student WHERE roll_no = 5");
  • mysqli_close($conn);
